claims.text: A roughly 5 µm PVD-deposited CrN/Al2O3 nano-laminated coating can be produced as an adherent coating on CoCrFeNi.
The coating will promote formation of a stable, self-regenerating lubricious tribo-oxide layer during sliding.
The tribo-oxide will remain protective throughout sliding from 25 °C to 800 °C.
Bare CoCrFeNi has acceptable room-temperature friction performance.
Bare CoCrFeNi suffers high friction and wear at elevated temperatures because of uncontrolled and unstable oxide formation.
Moderate substrate preheating at approximately 300 °C and controlled reactive-gas flow will produce a stoichiometric nano-laminated CrN/Al2O3 structure.
Post-deposition annealing will stabilize the coating–substrate interface.
The intended operating domain is dry sliding in air from 25 °C to 800 °C under moderate, service-like contact stresses.
The CrN/Al2O3 coating will form and sustain a continuous interfacial tribo-oxide containing protective Cr2O3 and Al2O3.
Frictional heating during sliding can activate reaction with atmospheric oxygen and generate a protective oxide layer.
Accumulated tribo-oxidation can create a protective oxide glaze that provides solid lubrication.
The proposed oxide glaze will have low shear strength and will replenish itself during continued sliding.
The tribo-oxide layer will limit direct metal-to-metal contact and thereby reduce friction and wear.
Relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi, coated specimens will have lower coefficient of friction and lower wear rate at every tested temperature from 25 °C to 800 °C.
Long-term coating performance may depend on adhesion and durability under thermal cycling and severe sliding.
Prolonged sliding and cyclic shear can fracture a protective oxide film into abrasive debris and accelerate material loss.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant reduction greater than 20% in both friction and wear relative to the uncoated control, or failure to confirm a stable continuous tribo-oxide, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as an 'oxide-based coating,' although the stated CrN/Al2O3 architecture is a mixed nitride/oxide laminate rather than wholly oxide-based.
